=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:247-349 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter in release_blocker_check_gate_failed (line 332) selects the newest failed gate run, including a `startup_failure` run, and report_release_blocker (line 248) sends that run's id as `--run-id` in `run_refs`.
  WHY: A startup_failure run has no jobs, so bind_report_claims (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3210-3216, FAILED_JOB_CONCLUSIONS at line 513) drops it as `run_not_failed` and returns `no_bound_runs`. scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:641 then calls `_report_auth_reject`, while the producer still logs `RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED`. No heal issue is filed and the Telegram WARNING never fires.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:513 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `startup_failure` is missing from `FAILED_JOB_CONCLUSIONS` (line 513), so a `startup_failure` gate run selected by `release_blocker_check_gate_failed` is reported to the intake, which cannot bind it because the run has no jobs.
  WHY: The intake rejects the report as run_not_failed. The producer logs RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED, but no heal issue or producer-side Telegram WARNING is ever sent for a release stuck on a broken gate workflow file.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:210-214 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `release_blocker_alert` (line 213) calls `tg_send_msg` synchronously, and that helper's curl has no request timeout (scripts/tg_helpers.sh:127-135).
  WHY: A stalled Telegram endpoint blocks the tick before the skip or release-gate dispatch, and the job's 10-minute timeout (.github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml:52) can kill the tick before the gate is dispatched. Severity disagreement: claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT; gemini, minimax and luna rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:131-134 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `tg_send_msg` runs `curl -s` with no request timeout, while its sibling `tg_send_report_msg` (line 163) uses `--max-time 30`.
  WHY: `release_blocker_alert` (scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:213) calls it synchronously before `skip_release`, so a stall can hit the 10-minute workflow timeout before the gate is dispatched. This contradicts auto_release_stable.sh:66 ("A reporter failure never fails or delays the tick").
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:355-512 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: release_blocker_check_stale never checks for gate runs on the tip, so it reports `stable_release_stale` on the in-flight path (489), the last_gate_failed grace path (504) and the dispatch/retry path (512). The test at tests/test_auto_release_stable.py:480 asserts this behaviour.
  WHY: The plan (docs/plans/release-blocker-heal-reports-plan.md:58) requires "no gate run started on the tip since". Age comes from max(tag time, oldest unreleased commit date), and promoted commits keep their `main` dates, so a normally progressing release is reported as stale. One blocker can also produce two heal issues with different fingerprints.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:266-292 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: If `request-report-identity` fails or writes no identity file, the reporter still wraps and dispatches an unsigned payload and logs `RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED` when the dispatch succeeds.
  WHY: For `release_in_flight` and `stable_release_stale` the payload has no failed-run references, and the intake (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2625-2654) skips reports without a verifiable reporter identity. The producer therefore records success although no heal issue is filed.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:283 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The new `gh_retry gh api -X POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" --input "${rb_envelope}"` call is not registered with the guard.
  WHY: The reviewer says this makes contract tests fail (test_dispatchable_workflows_match_the_gh_workflow_run_allow_rules, etc.) in tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, breaking CI contract compliance. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputed this finding and dropped it in their notes.
- .github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml:36 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow adds the privileged `id-token: write` permission to sign release-blocker reports with OIDC, and the reporter makes a `repository_dispatch` POST (scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:283).
  WHY: The permission broadens the workflow's ability to mint OIDC tokens, so its scope must stay tied to the heal-report dispatch. minimax judged the trust boundary consistent, with no new implicit-execution risk.
- tests/test_auto_release_stable.py:383 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: `assert f"RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED reason=last_gate_failed age=" in proc.stdout` is an f-string with no placeholders (ruff F541).
  WHY: The F rules are selected in ci.yml:377 and :665, so any `ruff --select E,F` run over the tests fails on this line.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:release_blocker_check_gate_failed, line 332; report_release_blocker, line 248 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A `startup_failure` gate run id is sent in `run_refs`. With zero jobs, bind_report_claims (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py lines 3210-3216, FAILED_JOB_CONCLUSIONS line 513) drops it as `run_not_failed` and returns `no_bound_runs`, and scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:640-641 calls `_report_auth_reject`.
  WHY: When the gate workflow file is broken, every 6-hourly tick logs `RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED reason=last_gate_failed ... run_ref=<id>` while the intake rejects each report. No heal issue is filed and the Telegram WARNING never fires. Fix: pass `--run-id` only for `failure`/`timed_out` and add a test asserting `run_refs == []`.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:release_blocker_check_stale (line 355 onward), call sites at lines 489, 504, 512; tests/test_auto_release_stable.py:480 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Staleness never checks for gate runs on the tip, which the plan (docs/plans/release-blocker-heal-reports-plan.md:58) requires. It runs while a gate is in flight, after retries, and inside the last_gate_failed grace window. Age uses the oldest unreleased commit's date, which keeps the `main` merge date.
  WHY: A normally progressing release gets a `stable_release_stale` report, and one blocker produces two heal issues (`blocker:stable_release_stale` plus the gate's failed-job fingerprint). Fix: return early when runs_json holds any gate run on `branch_tip` / `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_BRANCH`, and update the test at line 480.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:release_blocker_alert, line 213; scripts/tg_helpers.sh:131 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `tg_send_msg` is called synchronously, and its curl has no `--max-time` (the helpers at lines 163 and 224 use 30 and 10). TG_BOT_SECRET and TG_CHAT_ID are now bound in the workflow.
  WHY: A Telegram stall holds the tick at line 213, before `gh workflow run` on the dispatch path (line 512). The `timeout-minutes: 10` (.github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml:52) can kill the tick before the gate is dispatched.
- tests/test_auto_release_stable.py:line 383 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: f-string without placeholders (ruff F541; F rules selected in ci.yml:377 and :665).
  WHY: Any ruff run with `--select E,F` fails on this line. Fix: drop the `f` prefix.
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE. The missing "no gate run on tip" guard is reported under CORRECTNESS above.
- Notes: dropped pass-1 items: the tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py and tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py failures (not tied to any hunk), `id-token: write` (required by OIDC), and copilot-pull-request-reviewer `custom_instructions_too_large` (external).
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (3 related items): read `.conclusion` at line 332 and pass `--run-id` only for failure/timed_out (line 248, ~4 lines); return 0 in release_blocker_check_stale when runs_json has a run on branch_tip (~4 lines); bound the Telegram send at line 213 with `timeout 30` or `--max-time 30` (~2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml:permissions: id-token: write (line 36) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The workflow adds privileged id-token: write permissions for OIDC-signed release blocker reports.
  WHY: This broadens the workflow's ability to generate OIDC tokens; only the relevant dispatch should be signed and the scope must stay strict.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:FAILED_JOB_CONCLUSIONS (line 513) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `startup_failure` is missing from `FAILED_JOB_CONCLUSIONS`, so a `startup_failure` gate run is reported to the intake, which cannot bind it because there are no jobs.
  WHY: The intake rejects the report as run_not_failed. The producer logs RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED, but no heal issue or Telegram WARNING is sent.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:gh_retry gh api -X POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" --input "${rb_envelope}" | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new API call is not registered with the guard, so contract tests fail (test_dispatchable_workflows_match_the_gh_workflow_run_allow_rules, etc.) in tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py.
  WHY: Breaks CI contract compliance.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:release_blocker_alert (calls tg_send_msg, which lacks a curl timeout) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Telegram alert is sent synchronously, and tg_send_msg's curl has no request timeout.
  WHY: A Telegram stall blocks the tick before the skip or gate dispatch, and the 10-minute workflow timeout can end the tick before the gate is dispatched.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:line 332 combined with line 247-249 and line 332-349 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The jq predicate selects `startup_failure` runs and passes the id as `--run-id`. bind_report_claims (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3201-3216) drops the jobless run as `run_not_failed` (workflow_failure_heal.py:3212) and returns `no_bound_runs` (line 3215-3216), and workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:641 calls `_report_auth_reject`.
  WHY: The producer still logs `RELEASE_BLOCKER_REPORTED` after the dispatch succeeds (line 292), so the misleading success line hides the heal failure on every 6-hourly tick.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:line 213 (tg_send_msg call inside release_blocker_alert); line 210-214 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `tg_send_msg` is called synchronously with a curl that has no timeout, unlike the bounded background-send pattern in scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:759-786.
  WHY: A Telegram stall plus the 10-minute cap (.github/workflows/auto-release-stable.yml:52) can end the tick before the release-gate dispatch, breaking the spec's promise that "the gate is still dispatched after a stable_release_stale report".
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:line 213; release_blocker_alert (PERFORMANCE) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
